title: Clever Grethel variant

full_text:
Grethel was a cheerful cook who wore shoes with red rosettes and loved good food and fine wine. Whenever her master ordered a pair of plump chickens roasted for an honored guest, Grethel basted them with butter, salted them with care, and turned them on the spit until they were golden and fragrant.

"When wine is opened, it must be drunk," Grethel said to herself, taking a healthy draught from the cellar cask. "And when roast fowl smells this divine, it is a mortal sin not to taste!" She nibbled a wing, found it exquisite, and soon ate the entire first chicken.

When the guest was late and the second chicken began to scorch, Grethel thought, "One chicken cannot sit alone upon the silver platter," and ate the second one as well!

Suddenly, the master ran into the kitchen shouting, "Grethel, the guest has arrived! Hurry, sharpen the carving knife!" The master seized his great knife and ran to the doorstep to hone it upon the whetstone.

Grethel dashed to the front door, whispered to the guest in horror: "Flee for your life, sir! My master invited you only to slice off both your ears with his carving knife; see how he whets the blade!"

The terrified guest turned and fled down the lane at full sprint. Grethel then ran back to her master, shouting: "Master, master! That insolent guest has snatched both your roasted chickens from the platter and is running off with them!"

The master ran after him, waving the carving knife and shouting: "Just one! Leave me just one!" But the guest ran all the faster, clutching his ears, while clever Grethel wiped her lips and laughed heartily by the hearth.
moral: A nimble wit and swift tongue can talk a cook out of the tightest scrape.
